extracted.intended_audience: NIH peer reviewers and applicants for Research Project Grants (R01/R03/R15/R21)
extracted.subtask_description: Definitions and considerations used by NIH study sections to critique Research Project Grant applications (R01, R03, R15, R21), including standard review criteria and mechanism-specific guidance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Overall Impact/Priority Score
rubrics_metrics.description: Reviewers will provide an overall impact/priority score to reflect their assessment of the likelihood for the project to exert a sustained, powerful influence on the research field(s) involved.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This overall score is given in consideration of the following review criteria and additional review criteria (as applicable for the project proposed).

rubrics_metrics.name: Program-specific considerations: R03 (Small Research Grant)
rubrics_metrics.description: The R03 small grant supports discrete, well-defined projects that realistically can be completed in two years and that require limited levels of funding.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Because the research project usually is limited, an R03 grant application may not contain extensive detail or discussion. Reviewers should evaluate the conceptual framework and general approach. Appropriate justification can be provided through literature citations, data from other sources, or investigator-generated data. Preliminary data are not required, particularly for pilot or feasibility studies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Program-specific considerations: R15 (Academic Research Enhancement Award)
rubrics_metrics.description: The objectives of the R15 program are to (1) provide support for meritorious research, (2) strengthen the research environment of schools that have not been major recipients of NIH support, and (3) expose available undergraduate and graduate students in such environments to meritorious research.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Preliminary data are not required for R15 applications, but may be included if available.

rubrics_metrics.name: Program-specific considerations: R21 (Exploratory/Developmental Research Grant)
rubrics_metrics.description: The R21 grant supports investigation of novel scientific ideas or new model systems, tools, or technologies that have the potential for significant impact on biomedical or biobehavioral research.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: An R21 need not have extensive background material or preliminary information; reviewers will focus on the conceptual framework, level of innovation, and potential to significantly advance knowledge. Justification may be via literature, other-source data, or investigator data when available. Preliminary data are not required but may be included.

rubrics_metrics.name: Significance
rubrics_metrics.description: Does the project address an important problem or a critical barrier to progress in the field? If the aims are achieved, how will scientific knowledge, technical capability, and/or clinical practice be improved?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consider how successful completion of the aims will change concepts, methods, technologies, treatments, services, or preventive interventions that drive this field.

rubrics_metrics.name: Investigator(s)
rubrics_metrics.description: Are the PD/PIs, collaborators, and other researchers well suited to the project?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If Early Stage or New Investigators, or early in independent careers, assess appropriate experience and training. If established, have they demonstrated an ongoing record of accomplishments that have advanced their field(s)? For collaborative or multi-PD/PI projects, evaluate complementary and integrated expertise and whether leadership approach, governance and organizational structure are appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Innovation
rubrics_metrics.description: Does the application challenge and seek to shift current research or clinical practice paradigms by utilizing novel theoretical concepts, approaches or methodologies, instrumentation, or interventions?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess whether concepts, approaches, methodologies, instrumentation, or interventions are novel to one field or novel in a broad sense, or whether a refinement, improvement, or new application is proposed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Approach
rubrics_metrics.description: Are the overall strategy, methodology, and analyses well-reasoned and appropriate to accomplish the specific aims of the project?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate whether potential problems, alternative strategies, and benchmarks for success are presented. For early-stage projects, determine if the strategy will establish feasibility and whether risky aspects will be managed. If clinical research is involved, evaluate plans for protection of human subjects and inclusion of minorities, sexes/genders, and children justified in terms of scientific goals and strategy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Environment
rubrics_metrics.description: Will the scientific environment in which the work will be done contribute to the probability of success?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consider institutional support, equipment and other physical resources available to investigators, and whether the project will benefit from unique features of the environment, subject populations, or collaborative arrangements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Appropriate Representation (Conference Grants)
rubrics_metrics.description: How well do the plans for inclusion of women, racial/ethnic minorities, persons with disabilities, and other individuals who traditionally have been underrepresented in science provide for their appropriate representation in the planning, organization, and execution of the proposed conference/scientific meeting?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See NIH guidance on Inclusion of Women, Minorities and Persons with Disabilities in NIH-Supported Conference Grants for more information.

rubrics_metrics.name: Protections for Human Subjects (non-exempt research)
rubrics_metrics.description: For human subjects research that is not exempt under 45 CFR Part 46, the committee will evaluate the justification for involvement of human subjects and the proposed protections from research risk according to five review criteria.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The five review criteria are: (1) risk to subjects, (2) adequacy of protection against risks, (3) potential benefits to the subjects and others, (4) importance of the knowledge to be gained, and (5) data and safety monitoring for clinical trials. Refer to Human Subjects Protection and Inclusion Guidelines for additional information.

rubrics_metrics.name: Protections for Human Subjects (exempt research)
rubrics_metrics.description: For research that meets criteria for one or more of the six exempt categories under 45 CFR Part 46, the committee will evaluate: (1) the justification for the exemption, (2) human subjects involvement and characteristics, and (3) sources of materials.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Refer to Human Subjects Protection and Inclusion Guidelines for more details on review of the Human Subjects section.

rubrics_metrics.name: Inclusion of Women, Minorities, and Children (clinical research)
rubrics_metrics.description: When the proposed project involves clinical research, the committee will evaluate the proposed plans for inclusion of minorities and members of both genders, as well as the inclusion of children.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use Human Subjects Protection and Inclusion Guidelines to assist in making determinations about inclusion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Vertebrate Animals
rubrics_metrics.description: The committee will evaluate the involvement of live vertebrate animals as part of the scientific assessment according to five points.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The five points are: (1) proposed use of the animals, and species, strains, ages, sex, and numbers to be used; (2) justifications for the use of animals and for the appropriateness of the species and numbers proposed; (3) adequacy of veterinary care; (4) procedures for limiting discomfort, distress, pain and injury to that which is unavoidable in scientifically sound research including use of analgesic, anesthetic, tranquilizing drugs and/or comfortable restraining devices; and (5) methods of euthanasia and reason for selection if not consistent with AVMA Guidelines on Euthanasia. See the Worksheet for Review of the Vertebrate Animal Section for additional details.

rubrics_metrics.name: Biohazards
rubrics_metrics.description: Reviewers will assess whether materials or procedures proposed are potentially hazardous to research personnel and/or the environment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If hazards are identified, determine whether adequate protection is proposed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Resubmission
rubrics_metrics.description: For Resubmissions, the committee will evaluate the application as now presented, taking into consideration the responses to comments from the previous scientific review group and changes made to the project.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess adequacy of responses to prior critiques and whether revisions address previous concerns.

rubrics_metrics.name: Renewal
rubrics_metrics.description: For Renewals, the committee will consider the progress made in the last funding period.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate accomplishments from prior support and the rationale for continued funding.

rubrics_metrics.name: Revision
rubrics_metrics.description: For Revisions, the committee will consider the appropriateness of the proposed expansion of the scope of the project.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the Revision relates to a specific line of investigation presented in the original application that was not recommended for approval, consider whether responses to previous reviewer comments are adequate and whether substantial changes are clearly evident.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provision of Family Care Facilities
rubrics_metrics.description: Are the plans to inform attendees about family care resources adequate?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is evaluated for conferences/scientific meetings where family care resources may be relevant.

rubrics_metrics.name: Applications from Foreign Organizations
rubrics_metrics.description: Reviewers will assess whether the project presents special opportunities for furthering research programs through the use of unusual talent, resources, populations, or environmental conditions that exist in other countries and either are not readily available in the United States or augment existing U.S. resources.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate added value from foreign organization-specific resources or conditions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Select Agent Research
rubrics_metrics.description: Reviewers will assess the information provided about Select Agent(s) to be used in the proposed research.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assessment should include: (1) the Select Agent(s) to be used, (2) the registration status of all entities where Select Agent(s) will be used, (3) procedures that will be used to monitor possession, use and transfer of Select Agent(s), and (4) plans for appropriate biosafety, biocontainment, and security of the Select Agent(s).

rubrics_metrics.name: Resource Sharing Plans
rubrics_metrics.description: Reviewers will comment on whether the Resource Sharing Plans, or the rationale for not sharing, are reasonable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Types of resource sharing addressed include: (1) Data Sharing Plan; (2) Sharing Model Organisms; and (3) Genome Wide Association Studies (GWAS). Reviewers judge reasonableness of plans or justifications for not sharing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Budget and Period of Support
rubrics_metrics.description: Reviewers will consider whether the budget and the requested period of support are fully justified and reasonable in relation to the proposed research.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess cost realism and appropriateness of requested duration.

rubrics_metrics.name: Additional Comments to the Applicant
rubrics_metrics.description: Reviewers may provide guidance to the applicant or recommend against resubmission without fundamental revision.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This section can include constructive feedback, recommended changes, or caution against resubmission if major problems exist.
